Subject: Netflow & SIEM validation for VPC/on‑prem export

Hi Jane / Globex SecOps,

Following up on last week's intake: we're starting the validation phase for the private deployment export. Goal is to validate that your SIEM can accept (1) flow records (NetFlow/IPFIX), (2) app logs via a Splunk HEC endpoint behind your bastion, and (3) tracing hooks (OTel spans) forwarded from the collector.

To move fast, can you share the following by EOD Tuesday: 
- preferred ingest method for NetFlow (UDP collector vs. encapsulated push over TLS)
- public/bastion IP ranges and NAT behaviour for the collector hosts
- expected TLS mutual auth or token-only auth for Splunk HEC (if HEC: test token + endpoint URL)
- any required field mappings for netflow -> your SIEM ingestion (src_as, ingress_interface, samplers, etc.)

We'll attach a small sample NetFlow capture and a starter collector config from our side. On our checklist: retention metadata, chain-of-custody for evidence exports, and trace correlation (request_id propagation) for span stitching.

If helpful we can book a 30-minute lab session to exchange certs and run a short end-to-end test. Proposed window: Thu 11/30 14:00-15:00 PT.

Thanks,

Hiro Tanaka
Sr. Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
---
attachments: netflow-sample-20281128.log (netflow/pcap stub), collector-config-example.yaml (yaml stub)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@globex.com>

Date: 2028-11-28T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Netflow & SIEM validation for VPC/on‑prem export

Hi Hiro — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers: 
- NetFlow: we prefer encrypted push to a private collector behind our bastion (we avoid open UDP from internet).
- Bastion NAT ranges: 52.33.120.0/24 (egress), plus an internal CIDR for collector hosts — I'll send a CIDR spreadsheet in a follow-up.
- Splunk HEC: token-only auth for testing is OK; for production we require mTLS and our CA-signed certs. Test HEC endpoint: https://splunk-collector.globex.internal:8088/services/collector/event
- Field mappings: we'll attach a short mapping CSV. Typical required fields: host, source, sourcetype, event_time, flow_bytes, flow_packets, src_ip, dst_ip, src_port, dst_port, netflow_version

I attached the mapping and a short NetFlow snippet we use for parsing. We can do the lab on Thu 11/30 14:00 PT — secops will join.

Regards,
Jane
Lead SecOps Engineer — Globex Financial

attachments: globex-netflow-mapping.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-28T14:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Netflow & SIEM validation for VPC/on‑prem export

Thanks — adding a few internal notes and a proposed approach for the lab/test: 

1) Collector topology (recommended): 
   - Option A (preferred for Globex): upstream agent in customer VPC -> TLS push to Globex bastion HEC endpoint. Agent runs fluent-bit + flow-exporter shim.
   - Option B: UDP NetFlow receive on a dedicated private host inside Globex (requires inbound UDP firewall rules).

2) Auth & creds: 
   - For the lab, we'll send a temporary HEC test token (rotated after test). For production we will support mTLS; provide CSR process and we will sign with Redwood's intermediate for the collector if needed.

3) Tracing hooks: 
   - We'll instrument the collector to attach x-request-id and otel.span_id to exported events. Proposed sampling: 1% production, 25% debug per-service during onboarding. Need Globex to map trace_id->session_id in their SIEM for stitching.

4) Compliance evidence: 
   - We'll prepare a retention-and-custody-checklist.pdf that lists how long data is retained in the collector buffer, where snapshots are persisted, and an immutable transfer log for SOC2 evidence.

5) Test plan for Thu 11/30: 
   - Prework: exchange test token + CA certs, confirm bastion egress window.
   - Step 1: Push synthetic netflow file to HEC; validate sourcetype and timestamps.
   - Step 2: Push agent-sourced logs with trace headers; validate span stitching in SIEM.
   - Step 3: Verify retention metadata is preserved in exported artifacts.

I've attached a starter collector-config-example.yaml that sets TLS mode, batch size, and a sample grok for netflow. Marissa — can you include the snippet for the custody audit log format? Tessa I left two questions inline in the config about fallback routing.

-kim
Kimberly Park
Principal PM, Observability — Redwood Inference

attachments: collector-config-example.yaml
